questions.question: What is the main cause of different seasons on the Earth?

options.text: Earth's tilt and revolution around the Sun

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth's tilt and revolution around the Sun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Earth's axis is tilted at an angle of approximately 23.5 degrees relative to its orbital plane. This tilt is the primary reason for the occurrence of seasons.
 
• As the Earth revolves around the Sun, different parts of the planet receive varying amounts of sunlight at different times of the year, causing seasonal changes.
 
• When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences summer, while the Southern Hemisphere experiences winter, and vice versa.
 
• The equinoxes (around March 21 and September 23) occur when the Earth's axis is not tilted toward or away from the Sun, resulting in nearly equal day and night durations worldwide.
 
• The solstices (around June 21 and December 21) mark the longest and shortest days of the year, depending on which hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth's distance from the Sun:**

 
 
• The Earth's orbit around the Sun is elliptical, causing slight variations in the distance between the Earth and the Sun throughout the year.
 
• However, these changes in distance are not significant enough to cause seasons. For instance, the Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion) in January, during the Northern Hemisphere's winter.
 
 
 
• **Earth's rotation:**
 
 
• The Earth's rotation on its axis causes the cycle of day and night but does not contribute to the seasonal changes.
 
• The rotation occurs approximately every 24 hours and is unrelated to the Earth's axial tilt or its revolution around the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Solar flares:**
 
 
• Solar flares are sudden bursts of energy from the Sun's surface caused by magnetic activity. They can impact Earth's communication systems and satellites but do not influence the seasons.
 
• Seasons are a result of the Earth's axial tilt and orbital dynamics, not solar activity.

questions.question: Which biochemist was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1958 for his work on the structure of proteins, especially insulin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frederick Sanger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Frederick Sanger, a British biochemist, was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1958 for his groundbreaking work on the structure of proteins, particularly insulin.
 
• He was the first scientist to determine the complete amino acid sequence of a protein, proving that proteins have a specific structure.
 
• His work on insulin revealed its precise amino acid sequence, a discovery that significantly advanced the understanding of protein chemistry and molecular biology.
 
• Sanger’s research laid the foundation for the development of modern techniques in protein sequencing and contributed to the broader field of genetic research.
 
• He remains one of only four individuals to have received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry twice, the second being in 1980 for his work on DNA sequencing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rosalind Franklin**

 
 
• She was a British scientist whose work on X-ray diffraction was crucial in the discovery of the DNA double-helix structure.
 
• Franklin’s famous "Photo 51" provided critical evidence about the helical structure of DNA, which was later used by Watson and Crick in their model.
 
 
 
• **Eduard Buchner**
 
 
• Eduard Buchner was a German chemist who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1907 for his research on fermentation.
 
• He demonstrated that fermentation could occur in cell-free extracts of yeast, which helped establish that enzymes are responsible for biochemical reactions.
 
• Buchner’s work is considered foundational in the field of biochemistry and enzymology.
 
 
 
• **Carl Neuberg**
 
 
• Carl Neuberg was a German biochemist often referred to as the "father of modern biochemistry."
 
• He made significant contributions to the study of carbohydrates and enzymes and worked on the chemical processes of fermentation.

questions.question: In which Schedule are the forms of oath and affirmation for various constitutional offices specified?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Schedule of the Indian Constitution specifies the **forms of oath and affirmation for various constitutional offices**, such as the President, Vice-President, Ministers, Members of Parliament, Judges of the Supreme Court and High Court, and others.
 
• Oaths are essential to ensure allegiance to the Constitution and commitment to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.
 
• This schedule contains **specific formats** for oaths or affirmations to be taken while assuming office or performing official duties.
 
• It applies to several high-ranking officials, including the Union Ministers, State Ministers, Governors, Members of the Legislative Assemblies, and others.
 
• The forms of oath or affirmation ensure that every officeholder acknowledges their constitutional responsibilities and duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fourth Schedule:**

 
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the **allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States)** to different states and union territories.
 
• It specifies the number of representatives each state or union territory can send to the Rajya Sabha, based on their population.
 
• The allocation is meant to ensure proportional representation of states in the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Schedule:**
 
 
• The Fifth Schedule pertains to the **administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes** under Articles 244(1) and 244(2) of the Constitution.
 
• It outlines provisions for the governance, welfare, and protection of Scheduled Tribes in India.
 
• It also includes recommendations for the formation and functioning of Tribes Advisory Councils in states having Scheduled Areas.
 
 
 
• **Tenth Schedule:**
 
 
• The Tenth Schedule, commonly known as the **"Anti-Defection Law,"** was added to the Constitution in 1985 through the 52nd Amendment.
 
• It deals with disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection.
 
• The law aims to curb political defection by ensuring that elected representatives maintain loyalty to their party.

questions.question: Who predicted the existence of a new particle, now known as the neutrino, in 1931, using the conservation laws of energy and momentum for β-decay?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wolfgang Pauli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Wolfgang Pauli, an Austrian-born theoretical physicist, **proposed the existence of the neutrino** in 1931 to resolve the apparent violation of energy conservation and momentum conservation in beta decay.
 
• The neutrino was theorized as a small, neutral particle with **extremely low mass and no electric charge**, making it difficult to detect.
 
• Pauli's postulate was later **confirmed experimentally in 1956** by Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines, who detected neutrinos in a nuclear reactor experiment.
 
• The term "neutrino" was coined by Enrico Fermi, who **developed the theory of beta decay** incorporating Pauli's neutrino.
 
• Pauli's prediction of the neutrino is considered one of the most significant contributions to particle physics, as it laid the foundation for modern neutrino physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paul Dirac**

 
 
• Paul Dirac was a British theoretical physicist known for his work on quantum mechanics and quantum field theory.
 
• He formulated the **Dirac equation**, which describes the behavior of fermions and predicted the existence of antimatter (positrons).
 
• His contributions to quantum theory and particle physics earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1933.
 
 
 
• **Enrico Fermi**
 
 
• Enrico Fermi was an Italian-American physicist known as the "architect of the nuclear age" for his pioneering work in nuclear physics.
 
• He developed the first theoretical framework for beta decay, incorporating Pauli's neutrino, and named the particle "neutrino."
 
• Fermi also led the team that created the first nuclear reactor, the Chicago Pile-1, in 1942.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1938 for his work on induced radioactivity.
 
 
 
• **James Chadwick**
 
 
• James Chadwick was a British physicist who discovered the **neutron** in 1932, a subatomic particle with no electric charge.
 
• His discovery was crucial to the development of nuclear physics and the construction of nuclear reactors and weapons.
 
• For his groundbreaking work, Chadwick was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935**.

questions.question: Which index combines life expectancy, education and per capita income to measure a country’s human development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human Development Index (HDI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite statistic developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to measure a country's overall achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: life expectancy, education, and per capita income.
 
• Life expectancy is used to represent the health and longevity of a population.
 
• Education is measured through a combination of mean years of schooling for adults aged 25 years and expected years of schooling for children entering the education system.
 
• Per capita income is adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP) to ensure a fair comparison of living standards across countries.
 
• The HDI is published annually in the Human Development Report, providing valuable insights into global development and highlighting disparities between nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP per capita:**

 
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita is an economic metric that measures a country's economic output per person.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the total GDP of a country by its population.
 
• While GDP per capita provides an insight into economic productivity, it does not account for disparities in income distribution or other aspects of human development.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI):**
 
 
• The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures changes in the price level of a basket of consumer goods and services purchased by households.
 
• It is commonly used as an indicator of inflation and cost-of-living changes within an economy.
 
• CPI does not measure human development directly but is useful in understanding economic trends.
 
 
 
• **Gini Index:**
 
 
• The Gini Index, or Gini Coefficient, is a measure of income inequality within a population.
 
• It ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality).
 
• While the Gini Index provides insights into income distribution, it does not encompass other aspects of human development, such as health or education.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution specifically deal with the establishment of Tribunals for administrative and other matters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 323A and 323B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 323A** of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to establish administrative tribunals for disputes and complaints related to public services under the control of the Union or State governments.
 
• **Article 323B** allows legislatures at both the Union and State levels to establish tribunals for specific matters such as taxation, foreign exchange, industrial and labor disputes, land reforms, and more.
 
• These articles were introduced under the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, to reduce the burden on traditional courts and streamline adjudication processes.
 
• Tribunals established under Article 323A have exclusive jurisdiction, meaning disputes falling under them cannot be adjudicated by regular courts. Tribunals under Article 323B do not have exclusive jurisdiction.
 
• The Supreme Court of India, through various judgments like **L. Chandra Kumar vs Union of India (1997)**, has clarified the powers and limitations of tribunals established under these articles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles 32 and 226**

 
 
• These articles deal with the right to constitutional remedies and the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
• Article 32 empowers individuals to directly approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• Article 226 empowers the High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of fundamental and other rights.
 
• While these articles are pivotal for judicial review, they do not specifically address the establishment of tribunals.
 
 
 
• **Articles 356C and 360D**
 
 
• These articles do not exist in the Indian Constitution and appear to be incorrectly mentioned.
 
• For context, Article 356 deals with President's Rule in states and Article 360 pertains to financial emergency.
 
• These articles are unrelated to the establishment of tribunals or judicial mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Articles 14 and 15**
 
 
• Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of laws within the territory of India.
 
• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Although these articles establish the fundamental right to equality, they are not directly related to the establishment of tribunals.

questions.question: Which plateau is NOT a part of the Patland series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan Plateau.**__

__
 
• The Patland series refers to a group of plateaus located mainly in the Chotanagpur Plateau region of eastern India.
 
• **The Deccan Plateau is not a part of the Patland series and is a large plateau covering most of southern India.**
 
• It lies between the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats and forms the major part of the Peninsular Plateau of India.
 
• The plateau is mainly composed of basaltic lava rocks known as Deccan Traps formed due to volcanic activity.
 
• **Deccan Plateau**__
 __
 
• Location - Southern and Central India
 
• Boundaries - Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats and Satpura Range
 
• Formation - Volcanic basaltic rocks known as Deccan Traps
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Ranchi Plateau**__

 __
 
• The Ranchi Plateau is located in Jharkhand and forms an important part of the Chotanagpur Plateau.
 
• It is considered a part of the Patland series and is known for waterfalls such as Hundru and Dassam Falls.
 
 
 
• **Hazaribagh Plateau**__
 __
 
• The Hazaribagh Plateau lies in Jharkhand and is another important component of the Patland series.
 
• The region is rich in mineral resources such as coal and mica.
 
 
 
• **Malwa Plateau**__
 __
 
• The Malwa Plateau is located mainly in Madhya Pradesh and parts of Rajasthan.
 
• It is a volcanic plateau with black soil suitable for cotton cultivation.
 
• Major rivers draining the plateau include Chambal and Betwa.
 
 
 
• **Patland Series**__
 
 
• The Patland series consists of flat-topped plateaus located in the Chotanagpur Plateau region.
 
• These plateaus are generally located in Jharkhand and surrounding areas and are known for their mineral wealth.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025?

options.text: To restrict the establishment of new Waqf properties
To enhance transparency and inclusivity in the management of Waqf properties
To nationalise all Waqf properties under central government control and conduct an audit of new Waqf properties
To repeal the Waqf Act, 1995 and abolish Waqf Boards

questions.solution:

• It mandates the regular **audit of Waqf properties** and their management by independent agencies to ensure proper utilization of funds.
 
• The new amendments aim to encourage **public participation and inclusivity** by allowing representation from minority communities in decision-making processes.
 
• This legislation seeks to address long-standing issues of mismanagement, disputes, and lack of transparency in the administration of Waqf properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Waqf is an endowment made by Muslims for religious, educational, or charitable purposes.
 
• Waqf properties are governed under the Waqf Act, 1995, which provides for the establishment of Waqf Boards at the state level to oversee their management.
 
• India has over six lakh registered Waqf properties, making it one of the largest holders of such properties globally.

questions.question: Which policy was adopted by the British in the post-1857 revolt in India due to distrust of Hindu-Muslim unity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Divide and Rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The British introduced the **Divide and Rule policy** in India after the 1857 revolt to weaken the unity between Hindus and Muslims.
 
• This policy aimed to foster religious, social, and political divisions among Indians, ensuring that the people remained disunited and could not collectively oppose colonial rule.
 
• The British actively promoted communal differences by favoring one community over another in government jobs, education, and political representation.
 
• In 1909, the British introduced the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, which provided separate electorates for Muslims, further deepening communal divisions.
 
• The policy of Divide and Rule played a significant role in ensuring the British maintained control over India until independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Doctrine of Lapse**

 
 
• It was a policy introduced by **Lord Dalhousie**, the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
 
• Under this doctrine, if a ruler of a princely state died without a natural heir, his state would be annexed into British territory.
 
• This policy was one of the causes of the 1857 revolt as it alienated Indian rulers, including prominent states like Jhansi, Satara, and Nagpur.
 
 
 
• **Forward Policy**

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment granted constitutional status to Co-operative Societies in India?

• The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011** granted constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies in India.
 
• It inserted a new **Part IXB** in the Constitution, titled "The Co-operative Societies," to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies.
 
• Article **43B** was added to the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), emphasizing the promotion of cooperative societies.
 
• This amendment also brought changes to **Article 19(1)(c)**, ensuring citizens have the right to form associations, including cooperative societies.
 
• It aimed to ensure transparency, accountability, and empowerment in the functioning of cooperative societies, thereby strengthening the cooperative movement in India.

• Inserted **Part IXA** in the Constitution, titled "The Municipalities," and introduced Articles 243P to 243ZG.

• It introduced **Part IX** in the Constitution, titled "The Panchayats," and added Articles 243 to 243O.

• This schedule reinforces the principles of accountability and integrity in governance.

questions.question: Which movement marked Mahatma Gandhi’s entry into all-India politics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi's entry into all-India politics was marked by the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–1922).**
 
• Gandhi supported the Khilafat issue, which aimed to protect the Ottoman Caliphate, and combined it with the Non-Cooperation Movement to fight against British colonial rule.
 
• The movement was launched to oppose British policies, including the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, alongside the demand for Swaraj (self-rule).
 
• Gandhi encouraged Indians to boycott British institutions, goods, titles, and elections and adopt Swadeshi (indigenous products) and non-violent resistance.
 
• This was the first mass movement led by Gandhi at the national level, making him a prominent leader in Indian politics and uniting Hindus and Muslims under a common cause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement**:

 
 
• Launched by Gandhi in 1930, it was a key phase of India's struggle for independence.
 
• The movement began with the historic Dandi March, where Gandhi broke the British salt law by making salt at the seashore.
 
• It focused on non-payment of taxes, boycotts of British goods, and civil resistance.
 
• Unlike the Non-Cooperation Movement, it aimed to challenge British laws openly and systematically.
 
 
 
• **Salt Satyagraha**:
 
 
• This was a part of the Civil Disobedience Movement, initiated by Gandhi in 1930.
 
• It marked a direct protest against the British monopoly on salt production and taxation.
 
• The Dandi March symbolized the wider defiance of British authority and inspired numerous acts of resistance across India.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha**:
 
 
• Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was Gandhi's first major political engagement in India.
 
• It focused on addressing the grievances of indigo farmers in Bihar, who were forced into oppressive farming practices by British planters.
 
• Gandhi adopted non-violent methods to achieve justice for the peasants, marking his first experiment with Satyagraha in India.
 
• While significant, this movement was more localized and not a pan-India initiative.

questions.question: Vedantam Prahlad Sharma, born in Andhra Pradesh in 1923, was initiated into which of the following Indian classical dance styles?

• **Kuchipudi** is one of the major classical dance forms of India, originating in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance form derives its name from the village of **Kuchelapuram** in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its **graceful movements, expressive gestures (Mudras),** and intricate footwork.

• The dance is performed with intricate hand gestures, facial expressions, and music that includes Odissi classical compositions.
